pairs.locus: Seneca Maior, Controversiae 5.1 (Laqueus incisus, pars altera)
pairs.question: Cui me vitae reservas?
pairs.answer: Ut aedificem? aspice incendium. ut navigem? aspice naufragium. ut educem? aspice sepulchrum.
pairs.derivation: The declaimer asks for what life he is being kept alive and answers himself with a triad enumerating every purpose (building, sailing, raising children) and showing each destroyed (fire, shipwreck, tomb). Question taken verbatim; answer is the contiguous triadic self-response. Cut starts after the answering triad: it stops before 'In tam calamitosa domo feliciores fuistis...', which turns from answering to consoling the dead wife and children.

pairs.locus: Seneca Maior, Controversiae 5.6 (Raptus in veste muliebri)
pairs.question: Muliebrem vestem sumpsit, capillos in feminae habitum composuit, oculos puellari lenocinio circumdedit, coloravit genas. non creditis?
pairs.answer: Et qui non crediderant, victi sunt sponsione.
pairs.derivation: The descriptive sentences are kept as setup so 'non creditis?' has a referent (that the young man disguised himself as a woman); the question is the author's own rhetorical 'don't you believe it?'. He answers himself: even those who had not believed lost the wager. Answer ends at the first full stop; what follows ('Et hoc de sponsione forsitan venerit...') is a separate sentence elaborating, not part of the answer.
